eintraege.titel: Breaking even costs you money.
eintraege.text:
Breaking even costs you money.

A trade you close back at your entry still paid the spread on the way in and on the way out. Call it 0.2 % a round trip. Ten of those is 2 % of the position gone while your P&L column sits at zero and tells you nothing happened.

Scratches are not free. They are just quiet.

Send this to the friend who says he had a flat week.

How many scratches did you take last week? 👇

eintraege.titel: Your stop distance picks your position size, whether you meant it to or not.
eintraege.text:
Your stop distance picks your position size, whether you meant it to or not.

$10,000 account, 1 % at risk, so $100. If your stop sits 2 % away that is a $5,000 position. Move the stop to 0.5 % away and the same $100 buys you $20,000 of it.

Same risk on the spreadsheet. Four times the position in the market, four times the exposure to a gap, four times the slippage on the way out.

Send this to the friend who picks the size first and then looks for a place to put the stop.

eintraege.titel: Bet twice as much and your account stops growing.
eintraege.text:
Bet twice as much and your account stops growing.

At a 55 % hit rate with even money, the size that compounds fastest is 10 % of the account. Double it to 20 % and the long run growth rate falls to zero. Not slower. Zero.

Same edge, same trades, same order. Twice the size, and the curve goes flat.

Send this to the friend who sizes up after a good week.

What percent of the account do you actually risk? 👇

eintraege.titel: Waiting for confirmation turned a 3R trade into a 1R trade.
eintraege.text:
Waiting for confirmation turned a 3R trade into a 1R trade.

Entry at 100, stop at 98, target at 106. That is 3 to 1. Wait for the candle to close and you get filled at 102 instead. Same stop, same target, and the trade is now 1 to 1.

The setup never changed. The chart never changed. Your entry did, and it took two thirds of the reward with it.

Send this to the friend who always waits for one more candle.

What does confirmation actually cost you? 👇

eintraege.titel: You can be profitable and still have no edge.
eintraege.text:
You can be profitable and still have no edge.

30 green trades feel like proof. At a 55 % hit rate your true rate after 30 trades sits anywhere between 37 % and 73 %. A coin flip is inside that range.

To tell 55 % apart from a coin you need about 380 trades. Until then your equity curve is a sample.

Send this to the friend who went full size after one good month.

How many trades did it take before you trusted your numbers? 👇

eintraege.titel: At 100x, a 1 % move against you is your whole account.
eintraege.text:
At 100x, a 1 % move against you is your whole account.

$1,000 at 100x controls $100,000. The market dips 1 %, that is $1,000, and the position is closed for you. At 10x the same dip costs $100 and you are still in the trade.

Your stop 2 % away never gets the chance. The liquidation at 1 % comes first.

Send this to the friend who calls 50x "a bit of leverage".

What is the highest leverage you have ever used? 👇

eintraege.text:
Make 20 %, then lose 20 %, and you are down 4 %.

10,000 grows to 12,000. Then 12,000 loses 20 % and lands at 9,600. Do it the other way round, down first and up second, and you still land at 9,600.

At +50 % and −50 % the hole is 25 %. The swing itself costs money, whichever order it comes in.

eintraege.titel: 10 losses in a row at 5 % risk takes 40 % of your account.
eintraege.text:
10 losses in a row at 5 % risk takes 40 % of your account.

At 1 % risk the same 10 losses take about 10 %. And 10 in a row at a 50 % hit rate is 1 in 1,024, so across 2,000 trades you should expect it about once.

Getting back from −40 % needs +67 %. From −10 % it needs +11 %. Same streak, same hit rate. Only the risk per trade was different.

Send this to the friend who risks 5 % because "it's only 5 %".

How much do you risk per trade? 👇

Part 29 of the series.

eintraege.titel: Lose 7 of 10 and still come out ahead.
eintraege.text:
Lose 7 of 10 and still come out ahead.

Risk $100 per trade and take $300 when you are right. 7 losses cost $700, 3 winners bring $900, so the 10 trades close at +$200.

Same 10 trades at 1 to 1 and you are down $400. The win rate did not change. The payoff did.
